rules.desc:
Required Preparatory Coursework
Education Course Requirement: A minimum of nine units among three education courses (taken for a letter grade with a GPA of 3.0 or higher in those courses). Coursework completed for the Honors program in Education should address varied topics in the field of education, and must be approved by the honors director.

rules.name: Course Requirements
rules.desc: Students must enroll in EDUC 140 for a minimum of 1 unit in Winter and Spring Quarters.
rules.notes:
• Students are required to enroll in the Undergraduate Honors Seminar during their senior year: EDUC 199A (Autumn, three units), EDUC 199B (Winter, one unit), and EDUC 199C (spring, one unit)

• Students must enroll in Honors Research (EDUC 140) with their advisor during winter and spring quarters of their senior year. The number of units is determined in consultation with the faculty advisor.

rules.name: Thesis
rules.desc:
Upon successful completion of the honors program requirements, student theses will be posted in the GSE’s collection in the Stanford Digital Repository, a service supporting the long-term management of scholarly information resources at Stanford.
In addition to completing an honors thesis over their senior year, successful candidates for honors present brief reports on their research at a mini-conference held in spring quarter that all members of the academic community are invited to attend.

transferPolicy: External credit is not accepted toward the Honors Program in Education.
reviewNotes: Before honors you need at least 9 units in three education (EDUC) courses, letter graded, with a 3.0 GPA in them and the honors director's approval; the audit checks the courses and you check the GPA and approval by hand. You take the three senior honors seminar courses (EDUC 199A, 199B and 199C) and enroll in EDUC 140 with your advisor in both winter and spring, for at least 7 units in all. The honors thesis and its spring presentation are checked by the department.
